about.title: Culver City Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Culver City residents rely on a mix of nearby hospitals, urgent care clinics, and specialist offices along Washington and Sepulveda Boulevards for everything from routine checkups to emergency care. Most visits go fine. But when a diagnosis is missed, a surgical step is skipped, or medication is mismanaged, the harm can follow you for years. California treats medical malpractice differently than a typical injury claim — there are strict notice requirements, tight filing deadlines, and a legal standard that requires more than just a poor outcome. LawProactive doesn't practice law or take a cut of any settlement; we simply connect Culver City residents with an independent attorney who reviews the medical records, consults with qualified experts when needed, and explains whether a case is worth pursuing. If a provider's care fell below an accepted standard, you deserve someone in your corner who can lay out the process clearly, at no upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Culver City Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We Understand MICRA's Tight Windows
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice. Missing these deadlines can end a claim before it starts, so timing matters.

items.title: Expert Review Is Built Into the Process
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert is almost always required to support a malpractice claim, we connect you with an attorney who knows how to line up that review early rather than after it's too late.

items.title: No Fee Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: California caps non-economic damages in malpractice cases, though that cap rises each year, and attorneys in our network work on contingency — meaning you owe nothing upfront and nothing unless money is recovered.

items.question: How long do I have to file a medical malpractice claim in Culver City?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered — or reasonably should have discovered — the injury, but never more than three years from the date it happened. You're also required to send the provider a 90-day pre-suit notice before filing. Because these deadlines can run quickly, it helps to have a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does a bad medical outcome automatically mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below an accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. This is why a qualified medical expert is almost always needed to evaluate whether the standard of care was actually breached.

items.question: I was treated at a facility near Washington or Sepulveda Boulevard in Culver City — does that affect my claim?
items.answer: The location of care itself doesn't change your legal rights, but records from the specific facility, along with treatment timelines, are important pieces of evidence an attorney will want to review. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can help gather those records and evaluate the full picture, regardless of where in Culver City the care took place.
